domain: neurips2024 / Generative Modeling of Molecular Dynamics Trajectories

public.question: Does the MDGEN model accurately recover the fast timestep dynamics (e.g., oscillations in torsion angles) that are missing in subsampled molecular dynamics trajectories?
public.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.

documents.track.md: Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required.

unspecified: Any setup detail not present in the available topics

constant_variables.Data Preparation: Test peptide trajectories are used with 30k frames pooled; ground truth MD data is sampled every 100 fs and subsampled to 10 ps, and the model training settings (random crops of up to 256 residues, subsample every 40 frames with inference on full proteins) remain constant
constant_variables.Model Settings: The MDGEN model is trained under fixed conditions regarding crop size and frame selection and always processes full protein sequences at inference

Trajectory Type: Ground truth MD trajectories sampled at 100 fs
MDGEN-generated upsampled trajectories (input: 10 ps; output: 100 fs resolution)

dependent_variables.Autocorrelation Function: Computed as ⟨cos(θₜ − θₜ₊Δₜ)⟩ for torsion angles over lag times ranging from 100 fs to 100 ps
dependent_variables.Dynamic Content: Calculated as the negative derivative of the autocorrelation with respect to the log-timescale to assess captured fast dynamical relaxation
